blocks.content: This chapter catalogues J&K's major tourism destinations by name — a straightforward but high-value table-based memorisation chapter, building on the geography (Chapters 1-4), history (Chapters 5-8) and culture/religion (Chapters 20-21) content already covered.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The chapter categorizes key study areas into Major Tourist Destinations.
Adventure & Niche Tourism is highlighted as a specialized domain.
Includes structured Quick Revision Points for efficient review.

cells: Summer capital; Dal Lake houseboats/shikaras, Mughal Gardens (Shalimar, Nishat, Chashme Shahi), old-city heritage sites, Hazratbal and Khanqah-e-Moula shrines
Premier hill-station and ski resort; hosts the Gulmarg Gondola, one of the world's highest cable-car systems, and is a base for high-altitude trekking and winter sports
Scenic hill resort on the Lidder River; base camp for the traditional Amarnath Yatra route and popular for trekking, golf, and riverside tourism
'Meadow of gold'; gateway to the Zoji La Pass and Thajiwas Glacier; a base for high-altitude trekking towards Ladakh
Winter capital; 'City of Temples', including the Raghunath Temple; gateway to Vaishno Devi (via Katra)
Base town for the Vaishno Devi pilgrimage
Hill station and adventure-tourism destination on the Jammu-Srinagar highway route
Remote, recently-opened-to-wider-tourism valley near the LoC, prized for pristine scenery
Emerging, lesser-visited alpine meadow destination promoted as part of tourism diversification efforts

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Gulmarg's Gondola cable car is frequently cited as one of the highest-altitude cable-car systems in the world — a commonly tested tourism-infrastructure superlative for this UT.

items: Winter sports (skiing, snowboarding) are concentrated at Gulmarg, which has hosted national and some international winter-sports events, supported by its high-capacity Gondola lift system.

Trekking circuits — including the Great Lakes Trek (Kashmir Valley), routes through Kishtwar's high-altitude terrain, and approaches toward the Zanskar/Ladakh frontier via Sonamarg — cater to both domestic and international trekking tourism.

Houseboat and shikara tourism on Dal Lake and Nigeen Lake remains one of Kashmir's most iconic and internationally recognised tourism experiences, dating back to a colonial-era-origin tradition (houseboats were historically developed partly because non-state-subjects were restricted from owning land under earlier-era rules, prompting British and other visitors to commission floating residences instead).
Focus on identifying major tourist destinations and key geographical locations.
Pay special attention to niche and adventure tourism spots commonly asked in competitive exams.
Srinagar: Dal Lake, Mughal Gardens, old-city heritage; Gulmarg: premier ski resort with a world-class-altitude Gondola; Pahalgam: Amarnath Yatra base, Lidder Valley.
Sonamarg = gateway to Zoji La and Thajiwas Glacier; Jammu = 'City of Temples' and Vaishno Devi gateway (via Katra).
Gurez and Bangus Valleys represent newer, diversification-focused tourism destinations.
Dal Lake houseboat tradition has a distinctive historical origin tied to earlier-era land-ownership restrictions on outsiders.
